### 🌅 Sky, sun and clouds
- The sky is no longer a flat two-tone gradient — the horizon now glows warm on the sun's side at sunrise and sunset, and cools on the opposite side
- The ground no longer meets the sky at a visible line; distant terrain fades into the horizon seamlessly
- Clouds have been rebuilt from the ground up: real puffy shapes with lit tops and shaded undersides, in two layers drifting at different speeds. At sunset their undersides burn orange
- Night sky finally looks like one: a field of gently twinkling stars and a real moon, both fading in as the light drops
- The sun is now a visible disk with a wide warm glow, casting rays of light through trees and around buildings — most striking at sunrise and sunset
- Cloud shadows drift slowly across the survival landscape, dimming grass and terrain together as they pass
- **In survival, the day now actually plays out**: dawn and dusk sweep continuously through the sky, fog and light colors instead of the world being stuck in one fixed look — and night is genuinely dark, with dark fog to match
- Smooth sky gradients no longer show colored banding

### 💥 Hit feedback
- Damage numbers pop above whatever you hit — players, zombies, wildlife, turrets — with headshots called out in gold. Sustained fire merges into one number that counts up instead of flooding the screen
- Impacts now depend on what you hit: wood throws splinters and sawdust, stone chips and a lingering dust cloud, metal sprays hot sparks with a bright flash, flesh a burst of droplets and red mist, dirt clods and a dust puff
- Bursts spray *off* the surface you hit — out of a wall, up off the ground — instead of scattering in every direction
- Grenades and arrows also report their damage per victim, so a multi-kill blast reads as one number per body

### 🔫 Weapons up close
- The knife is a real fighting knife now: contoured grip with finger grooves, brass fittings and a lanyard loop, a clip-point blade with a polished edge, a blood groove and thumb grip notches on the spine
- The pistol got a sculpted slide with cocking serrations, an ejection port and glowing 3-dot night sights that line up when you aim. They ride the slide, so they blow back with every shot — and racking the slide on a reload now exposes the barrel and recoil spring instead of a gap
- The rifle gained the details you stare at all match: gas tube and block, cleaning rod, slant muzzle brake, stamped receiver dimples and rivets, selector lever, visible bolt carrier in the ejection port, tangent rear sight, palm-swell handguard and a proper stock with a steel butt plate

### 🧟 Creatures and nature
- Zombies have real hands — a flat palm with four curled fingers, a thumb and dirty nails — instead of a mitt with a claw. Hordes run just as smoothly as before
- Trees no longer look like stacked geometric shapes: lumpy canopies, ragged conifer branch layers, flared trunks with a natural bend, and roots
- New birch tree with dark bark scars

### 🎨 Graphics quality
- The game is now anti-aliased even with effects (bloom) turned on — no more jagged edges in the default settings
- Arena maps render every wall and building shadow at any distance; in survival, shadows follow you smoothly without flickering
- The daytime sun sits lower in the sky, so buildings and walls throw long, visible shadows instead of stubs
- Light bloom is softer and wider — glowing lights and muzzle flashes get a natural halo instead of a tight blur
- Walls and props on arena maps now darken subtly where they meet the ground, so they look grounded instead of floating
- Players and creatures cast a soft contact shadow, keeping them grounded even at night and in deep shade
- Arena ground and terrain gain subtle close-up texture instead of one flat color
- New "Ultra" quality option for high-end machines: sharper shadows and extra anti-aliasing
- Render resolution can now be pushed up to 200% for a supersampled, extra-crisp image
